deep.reconstruction:
Context (E260, §§36-41). Euler treats steady outflow of water from an upper vessel of section ff, kept full, through a broken canal of four straight pieces. The pieces have lengths a, b, c, d, widths f, g, h, i (so sections ff, gg, hh, ii) and inclinations giving vertical drops a, b cos ζ, c cos η, d cos θ. Water leaves by an orifice EE of section kk, and v is the height due to the outflow velocity.

Friction model. Friction is taken proportional to the pressure on the walls (a Coulomb-type law), with coefficient α. Along each piece the pressure height p then obeys a linear first-order ODE of the form dp/ds = -α p/width + (gravity and kinetic terms). Its integral over a piece of length a and width f gives a multiplier e^{-αa/f} on the entering pressure.

Recursion. The previous page writes e^{-αa/f} = 1-αA, etc., with A = (a/f)(1 - αa/2f + ...). It then propagates the pressure piece by piece (P, Q, R, ...), starting from the external (atmospheric) pressure height l at the free surface. It imposes that the pressure at the orifice is again l. This page completes that relation:

l(1 - 𝔄𝔅ℭ𝔇) = A𝔅ℭ𝔇 f + Bℭ𝔇 g cos ζ + C𝔇 h cos η + D i cos θ + 𝔅ℭ𝔇 𝔣 v + αBℭ𝔇 𝔤 v + αC𝔇 𝔥 v + αD 𝔦 v - v.

Here the abbreviations of §39 are 𝔄 = e^{-αa/f} = 1-αA, etc., and 𝔣 = k⁴/f⁴, 𝔤 = k⁴/g⁴, 𝔥 = k⁴/h⁴, 𝔦 = k⁴/i⁴ (squared area ratios).

Closed form (§39). Since the relation is linear in v:

v = [A𝔅ℭ𝔇 f + Bℭ𝔇 g cos ζ + C𝔇 h cos η + D i cos θ - l + 𝔄𝔅ℭ𝔇 l] / [1 - 𝔅ℭ𝔇𝔣 - αBℭ𝔇𝔤 - αC𝔇𝔥 - αD𝔦].

The total head is a + b cos ζ + c cos η + d cos θ.

First order in α (§40). Use A f ≈ a(1 - αa/2f) and 𝔅 ≈ 1 - αb/g, etc. The numerator becomes the head minus the terms
- αa(a/2f + b/g + c/h + d/i),
- αb cos ζ (b/2g + c/h + d/i),
- αc cos η (c/2h + d/i),
- αd cos θ (d/2i),
- αl(a/f + b/g + c/h + d/i).

The denominator becomes 1 - 𝔣 + α𝔣(b/g + c/h + d/i) - α𝔤 b/g - α𝔥 c/h - α𝔦 d/i.

Frictionless limit. For α = 0, v = q/(1 - k⁴/f⁴) = f⁴q/(f⁴ - k⁴), with q = AI the total height. This is the Bernoulli/Torricelli outflow corrected for approach velocity. For ff ≫ kk it gives v = q (§41), and the next page discusses the paradox v > q.

A notable feature of the model: because friction ∝ pressure, the atmospheric pressure height l enters the outflow velocity, through the term -αl Σ(length/width).
errors: No substantive errors in Euler's algebra. The closed form and the first-order expansion both check against the recursion of the previous page.
The model itself (friction proportional to pressure, so atmospheric pressure retards flow) is physically wrong for fluids. That is a known weakness of the paper, not a computational slip.

ideas.what: Pressure decaying exponentially along each pipe segment because friction is proportional to pressure; the multipliers e^{-α·length/width} compose multiplicatively over segments
ideas.modern_name: Linear first-order ODE / transfer-matrix (product) composition along a series pipe; Coulomb-type wall friction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (this paper); pipe friction later treated as pressure-independent (Chézy, Darcy-Weisbach)

ideas.what: Outflow height corrected for velocity of approach: v = f⁴q/(f⁴-k⁴)
ideas.where_published: E260 and Euler's hydraulic papers of the 1750s

ideas.what: Perturbative first-order-in-α expansion of the exact outflow formula

missed.claim: There is a formal analogy between Euler's segment-by-segment exponential pressure law here and his rope-friction (capstan) exponential law. Both come from friction proportional to normal force. The analogy is generic, and I am unsure whether commentators have remarked on it; it is not a significant gap.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historiographical interest: it shows Euler transferring a solid-friction (Coulomb/Amontons) law to fluids. That transfer is the physically flawed core of E260.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine completion of an algebraic elimination, plus a standard frictionless limit. The pressure-proportional fluid friction hypothesis is known from discussions of E260 and later rejected.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the first k⁴v term should be αB(1-αC)(1-αD)·k⁴v/g⁴ (not /h⁴), consistent with the Q and R expressions on the previous page.
§39 numerator: the last term should be +𝔄𝔅ℭ𝔇·l (pressure height l), not 𝔄𝔅ℭ𝔇𝔣; mathematically it must be l.
§40 numerator: '-αb cos ζ (b/2g + c/h + d/c)' should read d/i.
§40: the last bracket is '-αd cos θ (d/2i)' (closing parenthesis missing in print/transcription).
